description: The Hall of One Hundred Columns at Persepolis was one of the largest and most imposing buildings of the Achaemenid royal complex. Begun under Xerxes I and completed under Artaxerxes I in the 5th century BC, it featured a vast square audience hall supported by one hundred stone columns arranged in ten rows. Monumental doorways were decorated with reliefs showing the king, guards, and representatives of subject peoples, emphasizing imperial authority and the unity of the Persian Empire. It likely served as a grand throne or reception hall for royal ceremonies and official audiences.
